title: The Brothers Baker Swap Places in Catalonia
title_candidates: The Brothers Baker Swap Places in Catalonia
Alex Baker Wins the Trophy He Kept Nearly Losing to Himself
One Baker Rises, One Baker Falls: TEG 18 in Girona
theme: Two brothers travel to Catalonia in opposite trajectories and arrive at opposite ends of the leaderboard: Alex Baker converts three prior Wooden Spoons into a wire-to-wire Trophy despite authoring two of the loudest blow-up holes of the week, while defending double champion Jon Baker collapses to the Wooden Spoon itself.
opening_hook: Open on Alex Baker's Round 2 disaster stretch on the Tour course - a quintuple bogey at 16, a sextuple bogey at 18, and a round of 106 gross that stands as the worst round ever recorded there - before revealing he was still, at that moment, running away with the Trophy.

trophy_storyline.subject: Alex Baker takes outright control of the Trophy on Round 1's 5th hole and never surrenders it, surviving two personal collapses to win by 8
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: This is the whole Trophy story: a wire-to-wire leader whose floor never dropped below 3rd of 5 in any round, even while his own game briefly fell apart twice.
trophy_storyline.shape: Baker seized the outright Trophy lead for good on the 5th hole of Round 1 and built cushions of 12, 11 and 12 points across the first three rounds. In Round 2 alone he ran up a quintuple bogey at the 16th and a sextuple bogey at the 18th, the pair helping to a 106 gross that stands as the worst round ever posted on the Tour course - yet his Trophy lead did not blink. A tenth at the 14th in the final round barely dented an 8-point win over John Patterson, who for all his own recoveries could not make up a ruinous opening round.
headline_candidates: Baker Wins by 8 Despite the Worst Round in Tour Course History
Wire to Wire, Warts and All: Baker Lands the Trophy
The Steadiest Man in the Field Also Had the Worst Round in It
trophy_storyline.chosen_headline: Wire to Wire, Warts and All: Baker Lands the Trophy
trophy_storyline.standfirst: Alex Baker led the Trophy from the 5th hole of Round 1 to the last putt of Round 4, blow-ups and all.

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams climbs from a bottom-half Round 1 to win the Green Jacket by 14, overtaking Jon Baker's 20-hole lead along the way
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: The Jacket was built, not inherited: Williams got progressively better every round while the men above him did not.
jacket_storyline.shape: Williams opened poorly, three over the field's pace after Round 1, before a birdie at the 15th arrested the bleeding. He then improved in every single round - 27, 14, 13, 12 - overtaking Jon Baker's 20-hole Green Jacket lead early in Round 2 and going outright clear for good on the 2nd hole of Round 3. David Mullin, the closest challenger, actually shot the best gross round of the entire week to try to catch him and still finished 14 back.
headline_candidates: Williams Builds the Jacket One Round at a Time
From Three Adrift to Fourteen Clear: Williams's Green Jacket Climb
The Jacket That Got Better Every Day
jacket_storyline.chosen_headline: From Three Adrift to Fourteen Clear: Williams's Green Jacket Climb
jacket_storyline.standfirst: A poor opening round mended itself into a 14-shot romp, one improving round at a time.

spoon_storyline.subject: Jon Baker, the reigning Trophy and Jacket champion, collects the Wooden Spoon 23 points clear of the next-worst finisher
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: This is the tournament's sharpest reversal: last year's double champion becomes this year's bottom man, and by a distance nobody else in the field can rival.
spoon_storyline.shape: Baker arrived defending both the Trophy and the Green Jacket. He finished last in the field in three of the four rounds, swinging wildly between a 30 and a 39 without ever climbing into the top half, and closed 23 points adrift of David Mullin, the next-worst man. There was no single hole that did it - just four rounds that never came close to the standard he set twelve months earlier.
headline_candidates: The Defending Champion Finishes Dead Last
From Double Champion to Wooden Spoon in One Year
Twenty-Three Points Adrift: Baker's Fall Completed
spoon_storyline.chosen_headline: From Double Champion to Wooden Spoon in One Year
spoon_storyline.standfirst: Twelve months after winning both the Trophy and the Jacket, Jon Baker finished bottom of the field by the widest margin in the tournament.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin drops to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon race after a sextuple bogey at the Tour course's 15th, then two rounds later shoots a new course record on the Stadium
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The same player produced the week's worst single moment and, days later, the best round anyone has ever shot at that course - and it still wasn't enough to win anything.
discovered_storylines.shape: In Round 1, Mullin ran up a sextuple bogey 11 at the 15th and dropped to the bottom of the Wooden Spoon standings. By Round 3, on the tougher Stadium course, he shot 84 gross - a new course record, beating the old mark by 5 - only to still finish as Green Jacket runner-up, 14 behind Gregg Williams.
headline_candidates: Worst to Record-Best: Mullin's Wild Swing
From the Bottom of the Spoon Race to a Course Record
Mullin's Course Record Wasn't Even Enough for the Jacket
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: From the Bottom of the Spoon Race to a Course Record
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Two rounds after his worst hole of the week, David Mullin played the best round anyone has shot at the Stadium course - and still didn't win a thing.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson's second place, and the eight holes on the opening morning
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Patterson outscored the champion in two of the four rounds and still lost by 8, having gone 22 shots over par between the 3rd and the 10th of R1.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: an 8 at the 3rd in R1, then seven consecutive holes without a net par and 22 shots bled by the time he left the 10th green; he was bottom of the Spoon race by the 4th hole of the tournament (b23, b29, b18, b33). Turn: he spends the rest of the tournament hauling it back — 13 points across 13-16 to salvage R1, then 16 points over 11-15 in R2 despite another 8 at the 4th (SI 2) and 11 shots lost from the 6th to the 10th (b30, b11, b15, b32) — and sets personal bests at both courses along the way, 94 on the Tour in R2 and 93 at the Stadium in R3. Resolution: a birdie at the 17th in R4 halts one final slide (b03), and he finishes second, 8 adrift — a gap that had already been 12 before the first round was over.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Alex and Jon Baker's own inventories of blow-up holes are real and used as texture in their respective storylines, but the brothers' opposite-direction career swap - one shedding three prior Spoons for the Trophy, the other falling from defending double champion to the Spoon itself - is the more compelling frame this TEG.

why_the_champion_won: Alex Baker was the steadiest man in the field - never worse than 3rd of 5 in any round - while his closest rival, John Patterson, actually outplayed him in two of the four rounds but never recovered from a ruinous 22-shot Round 1 stretch; even an average round from Patterson would still not have caught him.
